items: A **constructor** has no return type and shares the class's name; `new` invokes it.
**Overloading** gives one name several parameter lists; the **signature** is name + parameter types, and return type is excluded.
Writing any constructor **removes** the free default one.
**`this(...)`** chains to another constructor in the same class and must come first.
**Static** members belong to the class and are shared; **instance** members belong to each object.
A static method cannot touch instance variables, which is why `main` needs an object.
